subject: cybersecurity
intro: Cybersecurity leads to the defenders, hunters and governors of digital systems — the people who detect intrusions, harden networks and write the risk rules everyone else follows.

roles.title: Information Security Analysts
roles.what: Plan, implement, upgrade or monitor security measures for the protection of computer networks and information — assessing vulnerabilities for security risks, proposing and implementing mitigations, and responding to breaches and viruses.
roles.where: Defensive operations and incident response, detection engineering and SIEM, applied cryptography, and the NICE-framework units map one-to-one onto this role's daily monitoring and hardening work.

roles.title: Computer Network Architects
roles.what: Design and implement computer and information networks — LANs, WANs, intranets and extranets — modelling and planning capacity, and researching and recommending the network hardware, software and security measures involved.
roles.where: TCP/IP for defenders, cryptography in practice with TLS and certificates, and cloud security's shared-responsibility models are the design material you will build architectures from.

roles.title: Network and Computer Systems Administrators
roles.what: Install, configure and maintain an organisation's networks, operating systems and servers — monitoring availability, reviewing logs, controlling user access, and managing backups, upgrades and software licences.
roles.where: Networking and OS internals for defenders, identity and zero trust from the emerging landscapes unit, and the governance strand's policies and baselines are precisely the systems and rules you administer.
